CORRECTION: An earlier commit (8eaffe0) claimed the model returns a byte-identical wrong answer every attempt and framed that as 'you cannot scaffold a representation the weights do not contain'. A second run of the same task refutes the determinism claim and weakens the general rule: attempt 2 of run 2 drifted to [710, 754, 703] (2 of 3 vectors correct) where run 1 stayed at [578, 578, 688] all three attempts. The model CAN move under feedback on this task; it just does not reach exactness. And a second, unrelated counter-prior convention (BGR channel order) passed on the first attempt.

corrected_findings: Single-run determinism claims are unsound: identical prompt, temperature 0.2, two runs, different output.
A local model can hold some counter-prior conventions on the first try (BGR packing: 1/1).
On the skill-verified Hilbert mapping it progresses under feedback (578 -> 710) but does not reach exactness; capability gradient, not categorical absence.
Practical rule unchanged for the builder role: no judgment-shaped or exactness-critical verification through a local model. The mechanism claimed earlier was wrong.
